title: System Status Report

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Time to put it all together, PROTO-7. Create a comprehensive status report using everything you've learned. This report will be our baseline diagnostic."
story.requirements: Your report must check multiple systems and use appropriate log levels to indicate their status.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Excellent work! This report clearly shows which systems need attention. You've mastered the basics of robot communication."

description: Create a comprehensive ship status report that demonstrates all Section 1.1 concepts: multiple log statements, various log levels, and console output.
requirements: Create a test case named 'Comprehensive Status Report'
Log a console message: 'Initiating full system diagnostic...'
Log 5 different ship systems with appropriate severity levels
End with a console message: 'Diagnostic complete'
constraints: Must use both Log and Log To Console
Must use at least 3 different log levels
All messages must be descriptive and realistic
instructions: Start with Log To Console to announce diagnostic start
Log status for: Navigation, Engine, Hull, Life Support, and Communications
Choose appropriate log levels based on system status
End with Log To Console to announce completion
hints: Think about which systems would be critical (ERROR), concerning (WARN), or operational (INFO)
Use specific measurements when possible (e.g., 'Hull integrity: 47%')
INFO is the default log level

theory.title: Section 1.1 Challenge: Integrating Core Concepts
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 stands before a large holographic display showing the ship's systems. Red, yellow, and green indicators blink across the grid.

"PROTO-7, you've learned the basics. Now prove you can use them together. Create a comprehensive diagnostic report that clearly communicates our ship's status."

What Makes a Good Diagnostic Report?

1. Clear Communication

Messages should be specific and actionable:

  • ❌ Bad: "System bad"
  • ✅ Good: "Hull integrity: 47% - damage in sector 7"

2. Appropriate Severity Levels

Choose log levels that match the urgency:

  • INFO: Systems operating normally
  • WARN: Issues that need attention but aren't critical
  • ERROR: Critical failures requiring immediate action

3. User Feedback

Use console output to show progress:

  • "Starting diagnostic..." at the beginning
  • "Diagnostic complete" at the end
  • Gives real-time feedback without opening HTML reports

4. Comprehensive Coverage

Check multiple systems, not just one. A real diagnostic covers:

  • Navigation systems
  • Power/engine systems
  • Structural integrity
  • Life support
  • Communications

Example Structure:

*** Test Cases ***
Full Diagnostic
    Log To Console    Starting diagnostic...
    Log    System A: Status    LEVEL
    Log    System B: Status    LEVEL
    Log    System C: Status    LEVEL
    Log To Console    Diagnostic complete

Challenge Requirements

Your diagnostic must:

  1. Check at least 5 ship systems
  2. Use INFO, WARN, and ERROR appropriately
  3. Provide console feedback at start and end
  4. Give specific status information (not just "ok" or "bad")

Think Like a Test Engineer

Ask yourself:

  • What would a rescue ship want to know?
  • Which failures are critical vs concerning?
  • How can I make the report scannable and clear?

MENTOR-9: "Show me what you've learned. Create the diagnostic report. If it's good, we'll know exactly what needs repair. If it's unclear... we might miss critical issues."

She steps back. "The ship's survival depends on accurate diagnostics, PROTO-7."

successCriteria: Uses INFO, WARN, and ERROR levels appropriately
Has console output at beginning and end
